sources.title: David Tong, Dynamics and Relativity, University of Cambridge Part IA Mathematical Tripos (Lent 2013)
sources.locator: §7.1–§7.4.7, printed pp. 107–145 (PDF pp. 113–151), read completely, including every subsection and the 'Electromagnetism Revisited' and 'Indices Up, Indices Down' passages

contents.name: 7.1 Lorentz Transformations (eqs. (7.1)–(7.6))
contents.support: Explicit coordinate form x'=γ(x−vt), ct'=γ(ct−vx/c); the pair keeps the design's x⁰=ct convention and states the same transformation laws.

contents.name: 7.1.1 Lorentz Transformations in Three Spatial Dimensions (final boost (7.6))
contents.support: The 4×4 boost matrix with y,z unchanged; used as the external template for the explicit Λ_β of the lemma.

contents.name: 7.1.2 Spacetime Diagrams; 7.1.3 A History of Light Speed
contents.reason: Diagrams, Rømer's and Michelson–Morley's historical accounts are physical/observational context for the SR track; this pair carries no observational claim.

contents.name: 7.2.1 Simultaneity (relativity of simultaneity; lines of constant t')
contents.reason: Relativity of simultaneity is observer synchronisation content of the SR track, not finite-dimensional Minkowski algebra.

contents.name: 7.2.2 Causality (light cone, future and past cones)
contents.support: Supplies the future/past cone terminology and the causal ordering context absorbed into the definition of C⁺.

contents.name: 7.2.3 Time Dilation (T=γT'; muon and Hafele–Keating tests)
contents.reason: Kinematical time dilation and its reported tests belong to the SR observer and experimental-interface pairs, not to this algebra pair.

contents.name: 7.2.4 Length Contraction (L=L'/γ; ladder-and-barn)
contents.reason: Kinematical length contraction is SR observer-measurement content; the pair asserts no rod or clock model.

contents.name: 7.2.5 Addition of Velocities ((7.9) and the |u|<c closure)
contents.reason: Velocity addition follows from the Lorentz group and belongs with the SR Lorentz-transformation pair.

contents.name: Twin-paradox discussion (accelerated worldline vs inertial worldline)
contents.reason: The accelerated-observer proper-time comparison is the SR proper-time-comparison pair's subject, with its own clock hypotheses.

contents.name: 7.3.1 The Invariant Interval ((7.11) and the timelike/spacelike/lightlike classification)
contents.support: The interval with the opposite overall sign is η; the classification dictionary is retained with the design's (−,+,+,+) convention.

contents.name: 7.3.2 The Lorentz Group (η (7.13), ΛᵀηΛ=η (7.14), boost (7.16), detβ²=1 splitting, proper SO(1,3), orthochronous SO⁺(1,3), rapidity)
contents.support: Supplies the matrix criterion, the detΛ=±1 split and the proper/orthochronous subgroup definitions used in the definition; the boost matrix is reused for the lemma.

contents.name: 7.3.3 A Rant: Why c=1
contents.reason: The c=1 unit convention is explicitly not adopted: the pair keeps the fixed positive c as separate structure as the design requires.

contents.name: 7.4.1 Proper Time (Δτ=Δs/c, dτ=dt/γ (7.18), T=∫dτ (7.19))
contents.support: The metric-speed integrand and its positivity along timelike trajectories; the pair proves the corresponding claims in the (−,+,+,+) convention.

contents.name: 7.4.2 4-Velocity (U=dX/dτ (7.20), U·U=c², four-vector transformation)
contents.support: U=dX/dτ with constant norm ±c² is the normalization clause η(U,U)=−c² of the lemma.

contents.name: 7.4.2 Addition of Velocities Revisited ((7.22)–(7.23))
contents.reason: The 4-vector velocity-addition and aberration formulas are SR Lorentz-transformation content.

contents.name: 7.4.3 4-Momentum (P=mU (7.24), E=γmc², P·P=m²c² (7.29))
contents.reason: Energy-momentum definitions and the mass-shell relation are the SR energy-momentum pair's subject, with its own mass assumptions.

contents.name: 7.4.4 Massless Particles (P·P=0; 'proper time is only defined for time-like trajectories')
contents.support: The explicit warning that proper time is defined only on timelike trajectories is absorbed as the null-case clause of the lemma; the photon/Doppler material goes to the SR light pair.

contents.name: 7.4.5 Newton's Laws of Motion (dP⁵/dτ=F⁵ (7.31); d/dτ(P·P)=0 for constant m)
contents.support: The conditional computation that the force equation with constant rest mass preserves the mass-shell norm is the model for the lemma's second clause.

contents.name: 7.4.5 Electromagnetism Revisited (G⁵_ν; dP⁵/dτ=(q/c)G⁵_νUᵛ; spatial part the Lorentz force)
contents.support: The antisymmetric tensor and the conditional particle equation mU'=qΦ(U) are exactly the lemma's hypotheses; the physical force law itself is a later physical premise.

contents.name: 7.4.6 Acceleration (A=dU/dτ, A·U=0; constant-acceleration hyperbola and Rindler horizon)
contents.reason: Four-acceleration and accelerated-observer horizons belong to the SR accelerated-observers pair; this pair is condition-free kinematics of the metric.

contents.name: 7.4.7 Indices Up, Indices Down (X_μ=η_{μν}Xᵛ; G^{μν} antisymmetric; dual-space remark)
contents.support: Supplies the raising/lowering convention Φ and the observation that it is the fully lowered two-form that is antisymmetric.

sources.title: Sean M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity (arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1, 3 December 1997)
sources.locator: Chapter 1 'Special Relativity and Flat Spacetime', printed pp. 1–30 (PDF pp. 8–37), read completely: the spacetime interval, the metric, Lorentz transformations, spacetime diagrams, vectors, the tangent space, dual vectors, tensors, tensor products, the Levi-Civita tensor, index manipulation, electromagnetism, differential forms, Hodge duality, worldlines, proper time, energy-momentum vector, energy-momentum tensor, perfect fluids, energy-momentum conservation

contents.name: the spacetime interval (1.3), s²=−(cΔt)²+Δx²+Δy²+Δz², and Minkowski space
contents.support: The interval is the quadratic form of η in the design's (−,+,+,+) convention, with c retained.

contents.name: the metric (1.8), η=ΛᵀηΛ (1.14), Lorentz group O(3,1), rotations (1.17), boosts (1.18), proper subgroup SO(3,1), Poincaré group
contents.support: The matrix criterion and the rotation/boost decomposition; the pair defines Lorentz maps abstractly and recovers the matrix identity by the congruence law.

contents.name: spacetime diagrams; light cones; future/past and timelike/spacelike/null separation
contents.support: Retained as the causal classification and the future cone C⁺ of the definition.

contents.name: vectors: tangent space T_p, basis ê_(μ), components, transformation V^{μ'}=Λ^{μ'}{}_νV^ν (1.25)
contents.support: Vectors transform by L, one of the transformation laws stated in the definition.

contents.name: dual vectors: cotangent space, one-forms, θ̂_(ν)(ê_(μ))=δ, components ω_{μ'}=Λ_{μ'}{}^νω_ν (1.37)
contents.support: Covectors transform by the inverse transpose, stated in the definition as θ'=(L⁻¹)ᵀθ.

contents.name: tensors: multilinear maps (1.44), tensor products (1.46), components (1.48), transformation law (1.51)
contents.support: The 'tensor = multilinear map, not an array' clause and the slot-wise transformation law of the definition.

contents.name: index manipulation: contraction (1.59), raising and lowering with the metric (1.61)–(1.62)
contents.support: Supplies the index-raised form Φ of a two-form used in the contraction lemma.

contents.name: the Levi-Civita tensor (1.57) and the 4-form ε
contents.reason: The Levi-Civita components and oriented volume four-form are already defined by def-oriented-minkowski-volume-form and their frame independence by lem-volume-form-is-independent-of-the-oriented-frame on sr-spacetime-primitives. The separate two-form Hodge/observer algebra is supplied by thm-sr-antisymmetric-observer-decomposition on sr-forces-and-continuum. The later electromagnetic covariance pair consumes these mathematical conventions under its own physical tensor dictionary; it is not their authoring home.

contents.name: electromagnetism: F_{μν} (1.58) with F_{μν}=−F_{νμ}; F^{μν} (1.75); Maxwell ∂_μF^{νμ}=4πJ^ν (1.77); dF=0 (1.91); potential F=dA (1.92)
contents.support: The antisymmetry of the field tensor is the structural fact the contraction lemma abstracts; the Maxwell and potential equations are deferred to the covariant formulation page.

contents.name: differential forms, wedge product, exterior derivative, closed and exact forms, de Rham cohomology, Hodge duality (printed 20–24)
contents.reason: Route only the used finite-dimensional two-form wedge/exterior-square and Hodge algebra to thm-sr-antisymmetric-observer-decomposition on sr-forces-and-continuum, using the earlier volume form on sr-spacetime-primitives. The used potential content has its earlier exact star-shaped and joint-regularity suppliers lem-em-joint-smooth-potentials on em-elementary-mathematical-prerequisites and pthm-em-spacetime-potentials on em-potentials-and-gauge; def-em-electromagnetic-tensor states F=dA when a potential exists, and pthm-em-tensor-maxwell-equivalence on em-lorentz-covariant-formulation supplies the explicit C1 cyclic closedness equations. This routing does not claim the source's general manifold exterior calculus, all-degree Hodge theorem, de Rham cohomology/Betti/Euler machinery, or unrestricted closed-implies-exact result as authored run content. Those unused source-specific extensions remain outside the approved inventory; all existing qualified algebra and potential claims remain intact.

contents.name: worldlines: parameterised curve x^μ(λ), line element (1.95), path classification, path length (1.96)
contents.support: Supplies the parametrised-curve and line-element picture absorbed into the C¹ curve hypotheses of the lemma.

contents.name: proper time (1.97): Δτ=∫√(−η_{μν}(dx^μ/dλ)(dx^ν/dλ))dλ, and inversion of τ(λ) to x(τ)
contents.support: The exact construction τ of the lemma, including the inversion step made rigorous there by the continuous-inverse and inverse-derivative theorems.

contents.name: four-velocity U^μ=dx^μ/dτ (1.98) and η_{μν}U^μU^ν=−1 (1.99)
contents.support: Unit normalization of the proper-time tangent is the c²-scaled clause η(U,U)=−c² of the lemma.

contents.name: energy-momentum vector p^μ=mU^μ (1.100)–(1.101) and E=p⁰
contents.reason: Energy and momentum of particles are the SR energy-momentum pair's subject with its own rest-mass and conservation assumptions.

contents.name: four-force f^μ=m d²x^μ/dτ²=dp^μ/dτ (1.102) and the electromagnetic force f^μ=qU_λF^{λμ} (1.103)
contents.support: The conditional equation mU'=qΦ(U) and the antisymmetry used to derive norm preservation; adopting it as the physical force law is a later postulate.

contents.name: energy-momentum tensor (1.106)–(1.112), perfect fluids, conservation ∂_μT^{μν}=0 (1.113)
contents.reason: Route the source's general symmetric stress tensor, dust (1.106), perfect fluid (1.107)–(1.110), scalar tensor (1.112) and their conditional conservation (1.113) to sr-forces-and-continuum: def-sr-stress-energy-tensor-and-force-density, lem-sr-dust-conservation-equivalence, lem-sr-perfect-fluid-conservation-equations and the scalar-field Hilbert/divergence suppliers. Separately, the electromagnetic specialization (1.111) corresponds, after the local SI/sign conversion, to pthm-em-covariant-stress-energy on em-lorentz-covariant-formulation, using the field balances on em-energy-momentum-and-angular-balance. No single EM destination supplies the compound matter row, and no conservation of an arbitrary symmetric tensor or matter dynamics from vacuum Maxwell is inferred.
